newsitem.title: USA: Cash crude prices falter in U.S., grade prices dip.
newsitem.headline: Cash crude prices falter in U.S., grade prices dip.

text.p: Bearish inventory data forced outright cash crude prices lower in the U.S. Gulf on Wednesday, while domestic grade barrels eased as well.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing talked late at $18.85-95 a barrel, around 40-45 cents lower than Tuesday.
Tuesday night's American Petroleum Institute data showed record crude imports of 9.2 million barrels per day, at the same time refinery utilization rates hovered around 98 pct.

Reports from the United Nations today focused on two Iraq-related events. First, a high-ranking Iraqi official said Baghdad would not start procedures to restart oil sales until monies sitting in an escrow account for buying humanitarian aid from previous oil receipts are exhausted. That accout holds around $800 million, possibly leaving new Iraqi sales some weeks off, according to diplomats.
U.N. chief arms inspector Rolf Ekeus also briefed the Security Council on recent standoffs between U.N. personnel and Iraqis who prevented inspections at sensitive sites.
Ekeus asked the council to condemn the Iraqi moves, but Baghdad complained that armed U.N. staff entered holy sites in the country, and generally infringed on Iraqi sovereignty.
Neither of the Iraqi stories could stop the steady selling seen on the NYMEX futures market, and subsequently in the outright price of cash WTI crude.
July Exchange for Physicals remained around an eight cents premium to the WTI/Cushing benchmark, with August levels pegged at premiums of two to six cents.
Grades saw Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James talk late at seven cents under the July WTI/Cushing, around four cents lower than Monday.
Midland/WTI moved late at WTI/Cushing -38 cents, West Texas Sour/Midland at -$1.25 and Postings Plus at $1.80-1.83.

Grades have seen a resurgence this week, trimming discounts to the WTI outright by some 20-25 cents for WTS/Midland and around 10 cents for LLS/St. James. Favorably "closed" arbitrage for bringing over North Sea Brent barrels underpinned sweet grades, but refiner ratable buying keyed much of the July barrel movement for all parcels.
"That refiner buying sort of faded away today," said a cash dealer.
